channel.title: Nissan recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Nissan Altima Passenger Air Bag May Not Deploy
item.description: Certain 2025 Nissan Altima vehicles may have had the front passenger air bag and the front passenger knee air bag installed with incorrect mounting fasteners. Because of this, these air bags may not deploy as intended if the vehicle is in a crash. This affects the front passenger seating position in affected vehicles, where both the main air bag and the knee air bag could be affected.

item.title: Nissan Armada and Infiniti QX80 Incorrect Weight Label
item.description: On certain Nissan Armada and Infiniti QX56/QX80 vehicles equipped with 22-inch wheels, the axle weight rating shown on the vehicle's certification label is incorrect. Because the number is wrong, an owner could load the vehicle beyond what it can safely carry. Nissan will correct the problem by installing new certification labels on the vehicle and mailing replacement labels directly to owners.

item.title: Nissan Sentra Driveshaft Issue May Cause Power Loss
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Sentra vehicles because the front left driveshaft may not be properly seated in the transmission. This can cause a transmission fluid leak and a loss of drive power. It can also allow the vehicle to roll away on its own if the parking brake is not set, since the driveshaft is not fully connected.

item.title: Nissan Kicks Software Error Can Blank Instrument Screen
item.description: A software error in the vehicle's combination meter, the display behind the steering wheel, may cause the screen to go partly or fully blank. When that happens, the screen can't show important information such as your speed or warning lights while you're driving.

item.title: Nissan Rogue Turbo Engines May Fail Or Catch Fire
item.description: In these Nissan Rogue vehicles with the 1.5L turbo engine, high engine temperatures can break down the engine oil. When the oil breaks down, the engine bearings can seize up and become damaged, which can lead to the engine failing. If a bearing fails badly enough, it can also cause a breach in the engine block, allowing hot oil to leak out of the engine.

item.title: Nissan Rogue Throttle Body Gears May Break
item.description: These Rogues are built with the three-cylinder 1.5-liter VC-Turbo engine. The electronic throttle body is the part that controls how much air reaches the engine when you press the accelerator, and inside it are small gears. Nissan says those gears can break. Dealers will reprogram the engine control software and will inspect the electronic throttle body assembly, replacing it if replacement is needed.

item.title: Nissan Altima and Sentra Doors May Open
item.description: Some Nissan Altima and Sentra vehicles have door strikers, the part that holds a door latched shut, that may have been welded incorrectly and could break. If a striker breaks, the door it's attached to could open on its own while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Nissan and Infiniti rearview camera may not show image
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain 2025 Murano, 2025-2026 Armada, and Infiniti QX80 vehicles. A software error in the infotainment system, the main screen in the dashboard, can occur when the vehicle starts up, and then the rearview camera picture does not appear when the driver shifts into reverse. Because of that, these vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility safety rule. A dealer can update the software, or the update can be sent to the vehicle over the air.

item.title: Nissan Sentra Windshield May Have Air Bubbles
item.description: Certain Sentra vehicles may have a windshield with visible air bubbles in the glass. These bubbles can block or blur the driver's view through the windshield.

item.title: Nissan NV200, Chevrolet City Express Fuel Pump Fuse Risk
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain NV200 vans, NV200 taxis, and Chevrolet City Express vans. In these vehicles, a wiring harness for a sensor near the fuel tank may have been routed incorrectly. Because of this, the wires can become damaged and cause a short circuit. That short circuit can blow the fuse that powers the fuel pump, cutting off power to it.

item.title: Nissan Leaf Battery May Overheat During Fast Charging
item.description: In these vehicles, the lithium-ion battery may overheat while it is being charged using a Level 3 quick charger. This can happen on vehicles equipped with a Level 3 quick charging port. Nissan will fix this by updating the battery's software, at no cost to the owner. Until this software update has been completed, owners are advised not to use Level 3 quick charging on their vehicle.

item.title: Nissan, Infiniti Engine Bearings May Fail
item.description: Certain engines in these vehicles use bearings that may have a manufacturing defect. Over time, this defect can lead to the engine failing. In some cases, a failed bearing can cause a break in the engine block, which allows hot oil inside the engine to leak out while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Nissan Kicks and Frontier backup camera screen may blank
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Frontier and Kicks vehicles because the center display screen may go blank when the driver shifts into reverse. That screen is where the rear camera image normally appears, so the driver may see nothing at all while backing up. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule for rear visibility. Dealers will update the software that runs the center display screen.

item.title: Nissan Kicks Certification Label Lists Wrong Weight Ratings
item.description: On certain 2025 Kicks, the certification label may show incorrect weight rating numbers, which could lead to the vehicle being loaded beyond what it can safely carry. Some SR trim vehicles with the optional 19-inch wheels may also have a label listing the wrong wheel size. This means the vehicles don't meet the required certification and tire standards.

item.title: Nissan Murano, Pathfinder, QX60 Brake Caliper May Break
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Murano, Pathfinder, and INFINITI QX60 vehicles because one or both front brake caliper assemblies may have reduced strength and could break while the vehicle is being driven. If a caliper breaks, the vehicle can lose front brake function on that side, making it harder to slow down and stop the vehicle.

item.title: Nissan Sentra Driver's Seat Frame May Be Loose
item.description: On certain 2025 Nissan Sentra vehicles, the driver's seat frame may not be fully secured to the outer side of the seat track.

item.title: Nissan Kicks Park Warning May Not Sound
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain 2025 Kicks vehicles because a warning that's supposed to alert the driver if the car is turned off while still in gear, instead of "Park," may not go off as it should. Without that warning, a driver could turn off and leave the vehicle without realizing it isn't in Park, and the vehicle could then move on its own.

item.title: Nissan Z Pop-Up Hood Sensor Wiring Problem
item.description: Certain Nissan Z vehicles may have the connectors for the right-side pedestrian detection sensors installed backwards in the front bumper wiring. This can prevent the pop-up engine hood from working the way it's supposed to in a pedestrian crash.

item.title: Nissan Rogue and INFINITI QX80 Rearview Camera May Go Blank
item.description: A software error can leave the rearview camera screen blank when the vehicle is shifted into reverse. Instead of showing the view behind the vehicle, the display shows nothing. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility standard that requires that image to appear. The fix is a software update for the screen system, which can either be sent to the vehicle over the air or installed by a dealer.

item.title: Nissan Leaf Battery May Overheat While Fast Charging
item.description: On certain Leaf models with fast-charging capability, the main battery can overheat while using a Level 3 quick charger. Nissan is fixing this with a software update to the battery, done by the dealer. Owners are being notified in phases, so letters may go out at different times.

item.title: Nissan Ariya Software Error May Cut Power
item.description: Some Nissan Ariya electric vehicles have software that helps control the electric drive system, and this software may sometimes incorrectly detect a problem that isn't actually there. When that happens, the software can shut down the vehicle's electric drive system. This shutdown causes the vehicle to lose the power it needs to keep moving while it is being driven.

item.title: Nissan Sentra windshield bubbles can hide the VIN
item.description: Some 2024 Nissan Sentra cars left the factory with a windshield that has air bubbles in the glass at the front lower corner on the driver's side. That is the spot where the vehicle identification number, or VIN, is displayed, and the bubbles can make the number hard to read. Because of this, the windshield does not meet the federal safety rule for vehicle glass. Dealers will look at the windshield and replace it if needed.

item.title: Nissan Ariya motor may lose drive power
item.description: On certain Ariya vehicles, O-rings inside the electric front traction motor may have been damaged when the vehicle was assembled. This can cause the motor to leak oil internally and lead to an unexpected loss of the power that drives the wheels. Losing drive power unexpectedly while driving raises the risk of a crash. Dealers will replace the front traction motor assembly at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Nissan Sentra Driveshaft Problem Can Cause Power Loss
item.description: On some Sentras, the front left driveshaft—the part that carries power from the transmission to the wheel—may not be seated correctly, or the clip holding it in place may be loose or missing. This can let transmission fluid leak out and can cause the car to lose power to the wheels while you are driving, so the vehicle may not move the way you expect.

item.title: Nissan Pathfinder, Infiniti QX60 seat belt pretensioner issue
item.description: On some 2024 Nissan Pathfinder and Infiniti QX60 vehicles, a part in the left front seat belt that tightens the belt in a crash may not be attached correctly. A rivet holding it in place is missing. Because of this, the seat belt may not hold the occupant properly if the vehicle crashes. Dealers will inspect the seat belt and replace it if needed.

item.title: Nissan Rogue Seat Belt Pretensioners May Not Restrain Occupants
item.description: On certain Nissan Rogue vehicles, the seat belt pretensioners for the driver and front passenger seats may have been manufactured incorrectly. Because of this, the seat belts may not properly restrain occupants in a crash, and the vehicles do not meet federal seat belt safety requirements. An occupant who is not properly held in place by their seat belt faces a greater risk of injury if a crash happens.

item.title: Nissan and Infiniti driver airbags may deploy improperly
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Nissan and Infiniti cars and SUVs because of a problem that happened during manufacturing. The inflator in the driver's airbag, which is the part that fills the bag, may absorb moisture. If that happens, the airbag may deploy improperly. Dealers will replace the entire driver's airbag assembly at no cost to the owner. Nissan mailed owner notification letters on April 10, 2024.

item.title: Nissan Leaf Rearview Camera Display Problem
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain LEAF vehicles because damage to the wiring for the rearview camera can cause the camera's display image to become distorted or disappear entirely. When the wiring is damaged this way, the vehicle no longer meets the federal safety standard for rear visibility. The problem affects the harness that connects the camera to the vehicle's display screen.

item.title: Nissan Murano Rear Side Glass May Detach
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Murano vehicles because the wrong primer may have been used on the quarter glass panels during assembly. As a result, the left and right quarter glass panels on these vehicles can detach from the vehicle.

item.title: Nissan Altima Steering Rack Bolts May Loosen
item.description: On certain Altima vehicles, the bolts connecting the electronic power steering unit to the steering rack may loosen. This can cause a loss of steering control or the steering to lock up.

item.title: Nissan Rogue Rear Brake Calipers May Leak
item.description: Nissan says the left and/or right rear brake caliper assemblies on some Rogue vehicles may be missing an internal bushing. This can allow the O-ring seal to move and brake fluid to leak out. Nissan is recalling the affected vehicles so dealers can replace the left and right rear brake calipers. Two vehicles previously inspected under an earlier recall that did not get a caliper replacement will need the new repair completed.

item.title: Nissan Z Pop-Up Hood Fasteners May Loosen
item.description: On certain Nissan Z cars, fasteners that hold a clip on the left side of the front bumper reinforcement can loosen over time. This clip is part of what allows the pop-up engine hood to activate, so if the fasteners come loose, the hood may fail to pop up and raise its rear edge the way it's designed to.

item.title: Nissan Ariya Software May Cut Drive Power
item.description: Some Ariya electric vehicles have inverter software that may incorrectly detect a short circuit. When that happens, the software shuts down the EV system, causing the vehicle to lose drive power.

item.title: Nissan Altima and Sentra rearview camera image may fail
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Altima and Sentra vehicles because the wiring for the backup camera can be damaged. If that wiring is damaged, the image on the rearview camera screen can come out distorted, or the picture can stop showing up at all. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal government's rear visibility safety standard. Dealers will look at the camera and the wiring and replace whatever is damaged, or protect and reroute the wiring.

item.title: Nissan Sentra Tie Rods May Bend and Break
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Sentra vehicles because the left and/or right tie rod, part of the steering system, may bend. If a tie rod bends, it can later break. This recall replaces an earlier recall for the same problem, so cars already repaired under that older recall will need this newer fix as well. Dealers will inspect the tie rods and replace any that are bent or broken, then later replace both tie rods with a newly designed part.

item.title: Nissan Kicks and Versa may lose power steering
item.description: Some 2021 Nissan Versa and Kicks vehicles have a wiring issue in the electric power steering system. An occasional bad connection in the sensor that measures steering effort can turn off the power steering assist. This recall also covers vehicles that were already checked under an earlier recall but never got their steering column replaced; those vehicles will need to be inspected again.

item.title: Nissan Leaf Risk of Unintended Acceleration
item.description: Nissan says some Leaf electric vehicles may speed up on their own, without the driver meaning it. This can happen if the driving mode is changed right after the driver turns off cruise control—for example, switching from "D" to "B," turning e-Pedal on, or picking "ECO" mode. That unplanned acceleration could occur while the car is already moving down the road.

item.title: Nissan Sentra Cowl Seal Leak May Corrode Wiring
item.description: Some Sentra vehicles have a missing or improperly fitted seal in the driver's side cowl area. This can let water leak into the vehicle and corrode electrical components and wiring. Nissan dealers will inspect and reseal the cowl, and if moisture or corrosion is found, they will replace the main wiring harness and engine room harness, all free of charge.

item.title: Nissan Rogue Rear Seat Belt Anchor Bolts Loose
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain 2023 Nissan Rogue vehicles because the fastener attaching a rear seat belt to its anchor point may not have been tightened properly at the factory. Over time, this loose fastener can loosen further. If a crash happens, a loose rear seat belt anchor may not properly hold a passenger in place, raising the risk of injury to that occupant.

item.title: Nissan Rogue, Pathfinder, Infiniti QX60 Seat Weld Failure
item.description: In some Nissan Rogue and Pathfinder, and Infiniti QX60 vehicles, the driver's power seat may not be fully attached to its frame. Over time, the welds holding the seat frame to a bracket at the back of the seat can come apart. If this happens, the seat is not as sturdy as it should be. In a crash, a seat that isn't properly secured may not hold the driver in place the way it's supposed to.
